env.world: A sharp bivariate boundary-discontinuity superpopulation model. A law \(P\) for \((Y(0),Y(1),X)\) with \(X\in\mathbb R^2\) and real potential outcomes is observed through the known Borel assignment regions \(\mathcal A_0,\mathcal A_1\subseteq\mathbb R^2\) with common compact boundary \(\mathcal B=\operatorname{bd}(\mathcal A_0)\cap\operatorname{bd}(\mathcal A_1)\): the treatment is the deterministic indicator \(T=\mathbf 1\{X\in\mathcal A_1\}\), the observed outcome is \(Y=TY(1)+(1-T)Y(0)\), and the observed unit is \(O=(Y,X)\in\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^2\). The sample \(\mathcal D_n=(O_i:1\le i\le n)\) consists of \(n\) independent draws induced by \(P\). For each side \(t\in\{0,1\}\) the one-sided restricted score measure is \(\mu_{t,P}(E)=P_X(E\cap\mathcal A_t)\), with closed support \(\mathcal X_{t,P}=\operatorname{supp}(\mu_{t,P})\); the side regression \(g_{t,P}\) is a Borel representative on \(\mathcal X_{t,P}\) of \(z\mapsto\mathbb E_P[Y\mid X=z]\) taken modulo \(\mu_{t,P}\), its boundary trace is \(\theta_{t,P}(x)=\lim_{z\to x,\ z\in\mathcal X_{t,P}}g_{t,P}(z)\), and the target estimand is the boundary causal trace contrast \(\tau_P=\theta_{1,P}-\theta_{0,P}\) on \(\mathcal B\). Local information is measured by the one-sided local-mass function \(q_{t,P}(x,h)=P\{X\in\mathcal A_t,\ d(X,x)\le h\}\) with \(d(x,z)=\lVert x-z\rVert_2\), by its two-sided minimum \(a_P(x,h)=\min_{t}q_{t,P}(x,h)\), by the thin-site packing profile \(\mathsf J_P(h,u)\) — the largest cardinality of an \(h\)-separated subset of \(\{x\in\mathcal B:a_P(x,h)\le u\}\), declared for all \(u\in[0,\infty)\) — and by the local effective multiplicity \(K_P(x,h)=1\vee\mathsf J_P(h,a_P(x,h))\). Fixed constants are the localization radius \(h_0\in(0,1)\), the Lipschitz and trace envelope \(L>0\), the known sub-Gaussian noise scale \(\sigma>0\), the mass constants \(0<c_m<C_m\), and the exponent range \(\kappa\in(2,\overline\kappa]\). Law classes are carved out of this world by member conditions: the polynomial-thickness class \(\mathcal P_\kappa^{\mathrm{base}}\), its isolated and pervasive thinning subclasses \(\mathcal P_\kappa^{\mathrm{iso}}\), \(\mathcal P_\kappa^{\mathrm{perv}}\), the declared modulus--lower-profile class \(\mathcal P(m,\mathsf J_-)\) built from a nondecreasing modulus \(m\) and a lower packing envelope \(\mathsf J_-\), and the triangular union \(\mathcal P_n(\Lambda_n)\) over declared triples \((\kappa,\mathsf J_-,\mathsf J_+)\).

env.world: The observable estimation layer over the model of \(\mathrm{S1}\), together with its decision-theoretic risk. Tuning is confined to the dyadic bandwidth grid \(\mathcal H_n=\{2^{-j}h_0:0\le j\le\lceil\log_2 n\rceil\}\). From the sample one forms the one-sided counts \(N_{t,n}(x,h)=\sum_{i\le n}\mathbf 1\{X_i\in\mathcal A_t,\ d(X_i,x)\le h\}\), the side-specific local-constant fits \(\widehat g_{t,n}(x;h)\), the count-qualified admissible set \(\widehat{\mathcal H}_{t,n}(x)\), the count-adaptive bandwidth \(\widehat h_{t,n}(x)\) with its deterministic tie-break and its \(h_0\) fallback, and the mass-adaptive boundary trace estimator \(\widehat\tau_n(x)=\widehat g_{1,n}(x;\widehat h_{1,n}(x))-\widehat g_{0,n}(x;\widehat h_{0,n}(x))\). Performance is measured by the expected-supremum minimax risk \(R_n(\mathcal P)=\inf_{\widetilde\tau_n}\sup_{P\in\mathcal P}\mathbb E_P[\sup_{x\in\mathcal B}|\widetilde\tau_n(x)-\tau_P(x)|]\), the infimum running over estimators measurable in \(\mathcal D_n\) and the known assignment geometry, and it is compared against the two frontier rates \(r_{n,\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso}}=n^{-1/(\kappa+2)}\) and \(r_{n,\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}=(\log n/n)^{1/(\kappa+2)}\).

env.world: The honest-inference layer. For a target simultaneous miscoverage level \(\gamma\in(0,1)\), a band is a data-measurable map \(\mathcal C_n\) sending each boundary location \(x\in\mathcal B\) to an interval in \(\mathbb R\), with half-width \(W_n(x)=\operatorname{diam}(\mathcal C_n(x))/2\). Honesty over a law class is simultaneous coverage \(P\{\tau_P(x)\in\mathcal C_n(x)\ \text{for every}\ x\in\mathcal B\}\ge1-\gamma\) (or \(\ge1-\gamma-\epsilon_n\) for a vanishing slack), and width is judged against the local thickness--entropy benchmark \(r_{n,P}^{\mathrm{loc}}(x)=\inf_{h\in\mathcal H_n}[2Lh+\sigma\sqrt{n^{-1}\log\{eK_P(x,h)/\gamma\}(q_{0,P}(x,h)^{-1}+q_{1,P}(x,h)^{-1})}]\). Distinguishability between two full observed laws is measured by the total-variation distance \(\operatorname{TV}(Q,Q')=\sup_E|Q(E)-Q'(E)|\).

env.world: The explicit witness and diagnostic geometry. Write \(\rho(z)=\lVert z\rVert_2-1\) for the signed distance to the unit circle, \(\mathcal T=\{z\in\mathbb R^2:|\rho(z)|\le h_0\}\) for the symmetric circular tube, and fix a site \(x_\star\in S^1\). On \(\mathcal T\) the two normalized score densities are \(f_\kappa^{\mathrm{perv}}(z)\propto\mathbf 1_{\mathcal T}(z)|\rho(z)|^{\kappa-2}\) and \(f_\kappa^{\mathrm{iso}}(z)\propto\mathbf 1_{\mathcal T}(z)\min\{1,(d(z,x_\star)/h_0)^{\kappa-2}\}\); the baseline witness laws \(P_\kappa^{\mathrm{perv},0}\) and \(P_\kappa^{\mathrm{iso},0}\) give \(X\) the corresponding density and set \(Y(t)=\sigma Z_t\) with independent standard normal \(Z_0,Z_1\), so both have identically vanishing side regressions and traces. Perturbed experiments are indexed by a maximal \(3h\)-separated set \(\Xi_h^{\mathrm{perv}}\subseteq S^1\) and the scale-dependent Lipschitz tents \(\psi_{j,h}(z)=(1-d(z,x_j)/h)_+\), with \(\psi_{0,h}\equiv0\): the laws \(\mathbb P_{\kappa,j,h}^{\mathrm{perv}}\) and \(\mathbb P_{\kappa,j,h}^{\mathrm{iso}}\) keep the score density and set \(Y(1)=(Lh/4)\psi_{j,h}(X)+\sigma Z_1\), \(Y(0)=-(Lh/4)\psi_{j,h}(X)+\sigma Z_0\). Two separate geometric diagnostics live here: the polynomial horn \(\mathsf H_\kappa=\{(u,v):0<u<h_0,\ |v|\le u^{\kappa-1}\}\), and, for a severity exponent \(\alpha>0\), the exponential horn mass modulus \(m_\alpha(h)=\int_0^h2\exp(-u^{-\alpha})\,du\).
